sanskrit_iast: ko addhā veda ka iha pra vocat kuta ājātā kuta iyaṃ visṛṣṭiḥ ... yo asyādhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman so aṅga veda yadi vā na veda
english_rendering: Who really knows whence creation arose? Perhaps its overseer knows—or perhaps not.
context_and_limits: Epistemic humility about cosmogony; not a rejection of teachers.

sanskrit_iast: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvato 'dabdhāso aparītāsa udbhidaḥ
english_rendering: May beneficial insights come to us from every direction.
context_and_limits: Openness to many sources; not specifically about guru authority.

sanskrit_iast: indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇam agnim āhur atho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān | ekaṃ sad viprā bahudhā vadanty agniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānam āhuḥ
english_rendering: Reality is one; inspired speakers name it in many ways.
context_and_limits: Supports plurality of formulation, not unrestricted relativism.

sanskrit_iast: saṃ gacchadhvaṃ saṃ vadadhvaṃ saṃ vo manāṃsi jānatām ... samānam astu vo mano yathā vaḥ susahāsati
english_rendering: Come together, speak together, and let your deliberation and intentions be shared.
context_and_limits: Collective deliberation; not anti-authoritarian.

sanskrit_iast: yadi manyase suvedeti daharam evāpi nūnaṃ tvaṃ vettha brahmaṇo rūpam ... atha nu mīmāṃsyam eva te manye viditam
english_rendering: If you think you know Brahman well, you know only a little; what you know still requires inquiry.
context_and_limits: Teacher corrects premature certainty.

sanskrit_iast: yasyāmataṃ tasya mataṃ mataṃ yasya na veda saḥ | avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ vijñātam avijānatām
english_rendering: It is understood by one who does not claim complete conceptual possession; one who thinks it fully known does not know.
context_and_limits: Paradoxical teaching on limits of objectifying knowledge.

sanskrit_iast: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ | dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ
english_rendering: Living in ignorance while imagining themselves wise, they wander like blind people led by the blind.
context_and_limits: Warns against false expertise and bad leadership.

sanskrit_iast: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena | yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām
english_rendering: The Self is not attained merely by preaching, intellect, or much hearing.
context_and_limits: Denies sufficiency of verbal learning; does not deny scripture or grace.

sanskrit_iast: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ | jaṅghanyamānāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ
english_rendering: Those in ignorance who imagine themselves wise wander like blind people led by the blind.
context_and_limits: Near-parallel of Kaṭha; counted in the same textual family.

sanskrit_iast: parīkṣya lokān karmacitān brāhmaṇo nirvedam āyān nāsty akṛtaḥ kṛtena | tad vijñānārthaṃ sa gurum evābhigacchet samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭham
english_rendering: After examining the worlds gained by action, approach a teacher who knows the tradition and is established in Brahman.
context_and_limits: Examination precedes approaching a qualified guru.

sanskrit_iast: ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyo maitreyi
english_rendering: The Self is to be heard about, reflected upon, and deeply contemplated.
context_and_limits: Hearing is one stage; reasoning/reflection is explicitly required.

sanskrit_iast: so 'haṃ bhagavo mantravid evāsmi nātmavit ... yad vai kiṃ caitad adhyagīṣṭhā nāmaivaitat
english_rendering: Nārada says, “I know the mantras, but not the Self”; Sanatkumāra replies that what he has learned so far is only name.
context_and_limits: Rote scriptural mastery is distinguished from realization.

sanskrit_iast: yāny anavadyāni karmāṇi tāni sevitavyāni no itarāṇi | yāny asmākaṃ sucaritāni tāni tvayopāsyāni no itarāṇi
english_rendering: Practice only our blameless and good conduct—not the rest.
context_and_limits: Directly limits imitation of the teacher: follow only conduct that is ethically blameless.

sanskrit_iast: atha yadi te karmavicikitsā vā vṛttavicikitsā vā syāt | ye tatra brāhmaṇāḥ saṃmarśinaḥ yuktā āyuktā alūkṣā dharmakāmāḥ syuḥ | yathā te tatra varteran tathā tatra vartethāḥ
english_rendering: If doubt arises about an action or conduct, look to thoughtful, competent, non-harsh people devoted to dharma.
context_and_limits: A communal procedure for resolving doubt; qualifications matter.

reference: MS B 432-7 v.193; other recensions differ
sanskrit_iast: yuktiyuktaṃ vaco grāhyaṃ na grāhyaṃ gurugauravāt | sarvaśāstrarahasyaṃ tad yājñavalkyena bhāṣitam
english_rendering: Accept speech that is joined with reason; do not accept it merely from reverence for a guru.
context_and_limits: Extremely direct, but verse number is recension-dependent; not safely “232” in all editions.

sanskrit_iast: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ | utpathapratipannasya kāryaṃ bhavati śāsanam
english_rendering: Even a guru who is arrogant, cannot distinguish right from wrong, and takes a wrong path must be corrected.
context_and_limits: Bhīṣma respectfully refuses Paraśurāma’s order in the Ambā dispute.

sanskrit_iast: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ | utpathapratipannasya parityāgo vidhīyate
english_rendering: Abandonment is prescribed for an arrogant guru who cannot distinguish right from wrong and follows a wrong path.
context_and_limits: A direct gnomic form in a statecraft discussion; parallel family.

sanskrit_iast: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ | utpathapratipannasya daṇḍo bhavati śāsanam
english_rendering: A straying, arrogant guru unable to discern right and wrong is subject to discipline.
context_and_limits: More severe statecraft variant; parallel family, not an independent maxim.

sanskrit_iast: iti te jñānam ākhyātaṃ guhyād guhyataraṃ mayā | vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru
english_rendering: I have taught you the most secret knowledge; reflect on it completely, then act as you choose.
context_and_limits: Krishna ends instruction by requiring reflection and leaving agency to Arjuna.

sanskrit_iast: tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā | upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninas tattvadarśinaḥ
english_rendering: Learn through humility, service, and sustained questioning of those who have seen truth.
context_and_limits: Supports respectful inquiry, not passive submission.

sanskrit_iast: īdṛśān aśivān ghorān ācārān iha jājale | kevalācaritatvāt tu nipuṇān nāvabudhyase || kāraṇād dharmam anvicchen na lokacaritaṃ caret ... upapattyā hi saṃpanno yatibhiś caiva sevyate
english_rendering: Do not fail to see harmful customs merely because they are practiced; seek dharma on grounds, not by copying the world; the wise honor what is supported by justification.
context_and_limits: Tulādhāra’s ethical critique of conventional sacrificial practice.

sanskrit_iast: uddhared ātmanātmānaṃ nātmānam avasādayet | ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
english_rendering: One should raise oneself and not degrade oneself; the self can be one’s ally or enemy.
context_and_limits: Supports personal responsibility, not a rule for evaluating scripture.

sanskrit_iast: upapattim upālambhaṃ bruvāṇaṃ sādhu rāvaṇa ... parīkṣitāḥ kṣipraṃ vināśam upayānti hi
english_rendering: Vibhīṣaṇa asks Rāvaṇa to weigh reasons and warns that unexamined undertakings quickly end in ruin.
context_and_limits: Practical counsel in war; thematic rather than a guru rule.

sanskrit_iast: guṇadoṣau parijñāya ... guṇavān vā yadi vā doṣavān ayam
english_rendering: Assess benefit and harm, then decide whether the newcomer’s qualities justify acceptance.
context_and_limits: Rāma’s council considers Vibhīṣaṇa; practical evaluation of a person.

sanskrit_iast: na tvevaṃ hi vicinvantaḥ ... pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yonir eva hi
english_rendering: Investigation uses observable signs and inference; judgment must be made from evidence.
context_and_limits: Hanumān argues that over-testing a sincere refuge-seeker can itself mislead; context matters.

sanskrit_iast: naitad yuktisahaṃ vākyaṃ hiṃsā dharmāya neṣyate
english_rendering: The claim that violence is dharma does not withstand reason.
context_and_limits: Spoken by Māyāmoha while deluding the demons; evidence of internal rational rhetoric, not the narrator’s universal doctrine.

sanskrit_iast: na hy āptavādā nabhaso nipatanti mahāsurāḥ | yuktimadvacanaṃ grāhyaṃ mayānyaiś ca bhavadvidhaiḥ
english_rendering: Reliable statements do not fall from the sky; reasoned speech should be accepted.
context_and_limits: Māyāmoha’s polemical speech; must not be isolated as the Purāṇa’s final doctrine.

sanskrit_iast: naitad yuktisahaṃ vākyaṃ hiṃsā dharmāya jāyate ... na hy āptavādā nabhaso nipatanti mahāsurāḥ | yuktimadvacanaṃ grāhyam
english_rendering: Ritual violence does not withstand examination; reliable claims do not fall from the sky, so accept reasoned speech.
context_and_limits: A parallel Māyāmoha recension; grouped with Viṣṇu Purāṇa witnesses.

sanskrit_iast: vṛddhāś cālolupāś caiva ātmavanto hy adāmbhikāḥ | samyagvinītā ṛjavas tān ācāryān pracakṣate || svayam ācarate yasmād ācāraṃ sthāpayaty api | ācinoti ca śāstrārthān ācāryas tena cocyate
english_rendering: A true teacher is mature, non-greedy, self-controlled, non-hypocritical and straightforward; one practices what one teaches and understands scripture’s meaning.
context_and_limits: Qualification test for an ācārya.

sanskrit_iast: dṛṣṭvānurūpam arthaṃ yaḥ pṛṣṭo naivāpi gūhati | yathādṛṣṭapravādas tu satyaṃ laiṅge 'tra paṭhyate
english_rendering: A truthful person does not hide what has been observed and speaks in accordance with observation.
context_and_limits: Definition of truthfulness; not specifically about a guru.

sanskrit_iast: śrutismṛtibhyāṃ vihito dharmo varṇāśramātmakaḥ | śiṣṭācārāviruddhaś ca sa dharmaḥ sādhur ucyate
english_rendering: Sound dharma is taught by śruti and smṛti and is not contrary to the conduct of the virtuous.
context_and_limits: This is a qualifying traditionalist criterion, not independent reason alone.

sanskrit_iast: āgamād anumānāc ca pratyakṣād upapattitaḥ | parīkṣya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā śraddhātavyaṃ vipaścitā ... cakṣuḥ śāstraṃ jalaṃ lekhyaṃ gaṇitaṃ ... pañcaite hetavo jñeyā jyotirmānavinirṇaye
english_rendering: The learned should examine carefully through scripture, inference, observation, reasoning, writing and calculation when deciding astronomical measures.
context_and_limits: Domain-specific epistemology: astronomy.

sanskrit_iast: calaty ekena pādena tiṣṭhaty ekena buddhimān | na parīkṣya paraṃ sthānaṃ pūrvam āyatanaṃ tyajet
english_rendering: A wise person does not leave one footing before examining the next.
context_and_limits: Practical prudence, not a theological rule.

sanskrit_iast: yo 'rthaṃ vicārya yuktātmā śrāvayed brāhmaṇān śucīn | sa doṣakañcukaṃ tyaktvā yāti devaṃ maheśvaram
english_rendering: One who carefully considers the meaning and teaches it with disciplined, pure scholars sheds error.
context_and_limits: Reflection on meaning is explicit, but the passage remains teacher-centered.

sanskrit_iast: bahutvād iha śāstrāṇāṃ jñānatattvaṃ sudurlabham | āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ || idam ekaṃ suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā
english_rendering: Because scriptures are numerous, truth is hard to obtain; churn all the scriptures and reflect repeatedly.
context_and_limits: Method is comparative; conclusion is explicitly Vaiṣṇava.

sanskrit_iast: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ | utpathe vartamānasya parityāgo vidhīyate
english_rendering: A proud guru who cannot distinguish right and wrong and remains on a wrong path is to be abandoned.
context_and_limits: Later Purāṇic witness of the Mahābhārata maxim.

sanskrit_iast: āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ | idam eva suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā
english_rendering: Having churned all scriptures and reflected repeatedly, the conclusion is to contemplate Nārāyaṇa.
context_and_limits: Quoted witness; close parallel to Narasimha Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast: tasmād yasyaiva saṃparkāt prabodhānandasaṃbhavaḥ | guruṃ tam eva vṛṇuyān nāparaṃ matimān naraḥ
english_rendering: A discerning person should choose as guru the one whose company produces awakening and joy.
context_and_limits: Outcome-based criterion for choosing a teacher.

sanskrit_iast: sa śiṣyair vinayācāracaturair ucito guruḥ | yāvad vijñāyate tāvat sevanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ ... na tu tattvaṃ tyajej jātu ... yatrānandaḥ prabodho vā nālpam apy upalabhyate | vatsarād api śiṣyeṇa so 'nyaṃ gurum upāśrayet
english_rendering: A seeker should assess the guru, never abandon truth, and if after a year no awakening or joy appears at all, seek another guru.
context_and_limits: Very direct, but the preceding chapter also strongly praises obedience; both contexts belong together.

sanskrit_iast: vṛddhāś cālolupāś caiva ātmavanto hy adāmbhikāḥ ... svayam ācarate yasmād ācāraṃ sthāpayaty api
english_rendering: Teachers are mature, non-greedy, self-controlled, sincere, and practice the conduct they establish.
context_and_limits: Parallel of Liṅga Purāṇa teacher-definition.

sanskrit_iast: vedavādaratā mūḍhāḥ karmaṇy eva pravartakāḥ ... na vidanti paraṃ tattvam
english_rendering: Those absorbed only in Vedic ritual words and action do not thereby know the highest truth.
context_and_limits: Narrative critique of ritualism; excerpt, and not a rejection of the Veda itself.

sanskrit_iast: naitat samācarej jātu manasāpi hy anīśvaraḥ ... īśvarāṇāṃ vacaḥ satyaṃ tathaivācaritaṃ kvacit | teṣāṃ yat svavacoyuktaṃ buddhimāṃs tat samācaret
english_rendering: One without divine mastery must not imitate extraordinary divine acts; the intelligent follow only conduct consistent with the deity’s own teaching.
context_and_limits: Directly rejects “a god did it, therefore imitate it.”

sanskrit_iast: balir evaṃ gṛhapatiḥ kulācāryeṇa bhāṣitaḥ | tūṣṇīṃ bhūtvā kṣaṇaṃ rājan uvācāvahito gurum ... na hy asatyāt paro 'dharmaḥ
english_rendering: Bali pauses and considers his family guru’s advice, then rejects it because he judges falsehood the greater adharma.
context_and_limits: Narrative dissent from Śukra, grounded in truthfulness.

sanskrit_iast: śrī-balir uvāca ... nāhaṃ bibhemi nirayān nādhanyād asukhārṇavāt | na sthānacyavanān mṛtyor yathā viprapralambhanāt
english_rendering: Bali explains that he fears deceiving a brāhmaṇa more than hell, poverty, loss of position, or death, so he will not retract his promise.
context_and_limits: Continuation of the Bali episode; truth and vow override the teacher’s prudential command.

sanskrit_iast: guruṇā bhartsitaḥ śapto jahau satyaṃ na suvrataḥ | chalair ukto mayā dharmo nāyaṃ tyajati satyavāk
english_rendering: Though rebuked and cursed by his guru, the steadfast Bali did not abandon truth.
context_and_limits: The divine narrator praises Bali’s refusal to lie.

sanskrit_iast: nimeś cacāra dehaṃ svaṃ gurave 'dharmavartine | gurur apy apatad dehe lobhād dharmam ajānataḥ
english_rendering: Nimi condemns his guru for acting contrary to dharma through greed and failing to discern dharma.
context_and_limits: Conflict narrative; closely related to the Viṣṇu Purāṇa Nimi story.

sanskrit_iast: tasmād guruṃ prapadyeta jijñāsuḥ śreya uttamam | śābde pare ca niṣṇātaṃ brahmaṇy upaśamāśrayam
english_rendering: A seeker should approach a guru deeply grounded in scripture and realization, and established in peace.
context_and_limits: Qualification criteria imply that not every claimant is a guru.

sanskrit_iast: aṇubhyaś ca mahadbhyaś ca śāstrebhyaḥ kuśalo naraḥ | sarvataḥ sāram ādadyāt puṣpebhya iva ṣaṭpadaḥ
english_rendering: A skillful person takes the essence from teachings small and great, like a bee taking nectar from many flowers.
context_and_limits: Comparative learning from multiple texts.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ gurubhya etebhya eṣā me śikṣitā matiḥ | svātmopaśikṣitāṃ buddhiṃ śṛṇu me ... deho gurur mama viraktivivekahetuḥ
english_rendering: I learned from these many teachers and from my own body and discernment; the body itself became a teacher of detachment.
context_and_limits: Avadhūta’s twenty-four teachers and experiential reflection.

sanskrit_iast: na hy ekasmād guror jñānaṃ susthiraṃ syāt supuṣkalam | brahmaitad advitīyaṃ vai gīyate bahudharṣibhiḥ
english_rendering: Firm and abundant knowledge does not arise from one guru alone; sages express the one reality in many ways.
context_and_limits: Directly denies monopoly by one teacher; not a rejection of initiation traditions.

sanskrit_iast: śrutiḥ pratyakṣam aitihyam anumānaṃ catuṣṭayam | pramāṇeṣv anavasthānād vikalpāt sa virajyate
english_rendering: Scripture, perception, tradition, and inference form a fourfold evidential field; their alternatives can produce dispassion from fixed constructions.
context_and_limits: Translation is interpretively difficult; not simply “all sources are equal.”

sanskrit_iast: paurvāparyam ato 'mīṣāṃ prasaṅkhyānam abhīpsatām | yathā viviktaṃ yad vaktraṃ gṛhṇīmo yuktisambhavāt
english_rendering: Among differing analyses, we accept the account that can be distinctly established through reasoning.
context_and_limits: Speaker-sensitive grammar is debated; the verse unmistakably invokes yukti.

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣeṇānumānena nigamenātmasaṃvidā | ādyantavad asaj jñātvā niḥsaṅgo vicared iha
english_rendering: Through perception, inference, scripture, and inner realization, discern the conditioned world’s transience.
context_and_limits: Multiple coordinated modes of knowing.

sanskrit_iast: jñānaṃ viveko nigamas tapaś ca pratyakṣam aitihyam athānumānam | ādyantayor asya yad eva kevalaṃ kālaś ca hetuś ca tad eva madhye
english_rendering: Knowledge, discrimination, scripture, discipline, perception, tradition, inference, time and causation contribute to discernment.
context_and_limits: Metaphysical context; not a general modern scientific method.

sanskrit_iast: nivṛttaṃ karma seveta pravṛttaṃ matparas tyajet | jijñāsāyāṃ sampravṛtto nādriyeta karmacodanām
english_rendering: One engaged in inquiry into the highest truth is no longer bound to injunctions aimed at ordinary fruitive action.
context_and_limits: Applies to an advanced seeker, not a blanket rejection of ethical rules.

sanskrit_iast: iti te bhagavadyācñāṃ śṛṇvanto 'pi na śuśruvuḥ | kṣudrāśā bhūrikarmāṇo bāliśā vṛddhamāninaḥ
english_rendering: Ritualists proud of age and many rites ignore the divine request and are called foolish.
context_and_limits: Status, age, and ritual volume do not guarantee wisdom.

sanskrit_iast: matir na kṛṣṇe parataḥ svato vā ... andhā yathāndhair upanīyamānās te 'pīśatantryām urudāmni baddhāḥ
english_rendering: Those led by leaders who are themselves blind remain bound, like blind people led by the blind.
context_and_limits: Sectarian devotional context; strong image against unqualified leadership.

sanskrit_iast: gurur na sa syāt svajano na sa syāt pitā na sa syāj jananī na sā syāt | daivaṃ na tat syān na patiś ca sa syān na mocayed yaḥ samupetamṛtyum
english_rendering: One should not assume the role of guru, kin, parent, deity, or spouse if unable to lead the dependent beyond death.
context_and_limits: Sets a demanding functional qualification; not permission to disregard any imperfect teacher.

sanskrit_iast: tato nimeḥ śāpo 'bhūd duṣṭaguroḥ ...
english_rendering: Nimi’s conflict identifies a guru as blameworthy when greed and misconduct displace duty.
context_and_limits: Parallel Nimi–Vasiṣṭha narrative; wording differs by edition.

sanskrit_iast: śāstrārthajñaṃ guruṃ prāpya vicāraṃ ca samācaret ...
english_rendering: After finding a teacher who knows scripture, the student should undertake reflection.
context_and_limits: Context remains strongly traditional and subordinates free-standing tarka; included as a qualified parallel.

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣaṃ cānumānaṃ ca śāstraṃ ca vividhāgamam | trayaṃ suviditaṃ kāryaṃ dharmaśuddhim abhīpsatā || ārṣaṃ dharmopadeśaṃ ca vedaśāstrāvirodhinā | yas tarkeṇānusaṃdhatte sa dharmaṃ veda netaraḥ
english_rendering: One seeking clarity in dharma must know perception, inference, and diverse scripture; one truly knows dharma by investigating the sages’ teaching with reasoning that does not contradict Veda.
context_and_limits: A strong synthesis, but reason is expressly bounded by Vedic consistency.

sanskrit_iast: dharmaśāstrārthaśāstrābhyām avirodhena pārthivaḥ | samīkṣamāṇo nipuṇaṃ vyavahāragatiṃ nayet
english_rendering: A ruler should determine legal procedure through careful examination consistent with Dharmaśāstra and Arthaśāstra.
context_and_limits: Judicial method, not theology.

sanskrit_iast: kevalaṃ śāstram āśritya na kartavyo vinirṇayaḥ | yuktihīne vicāre tu dharmahāniḥ prajāyate
english_rendering: A decision must not be made by relying on scripture alone; when inquiry lacks reasoning, dharma is harmed.
context_and_limits: One of the clearest direct statements, specifically in adjudication.

sanskrit_iast: cauro 'cauraḥ sādhv asādhu jāyate vyavahārataḥ | yuktiṃ vinā vicāreṇa māṇḍavyaś coratāṃ gataḥ
english_rendering: In litigation the innocent can be made a thief and the good made bad; without reasoning in inquiry, Māṇḍavya was condemned as a thief.
context_and_limits: Warns concretely against authority acting without rational evaluation.

sanskrit_iast: asatyāḥ satyasadṛśāḥ satyāś cāsatyasaṃnibhāḥ | dṛśyante bhrāntijanakās tasmād yuktyā vicārayet
english_rendering: False claims may look true and true claims false; because appearances mislead, one should investigate through reasoning.
context_and_limits: Judicial epistemology with general force.

sanskrit_iast: na dharmādharmau carata āvaṃ sva iti | na devagandharvā na pitara ity ācakṣate 'yaṃ dharmo 'yam adharma iti | yat tv āryāḥ kriyamāṇaṃ praśaṃsanti sa dharmo yad garhante so 'dharmaḥ | ... samyagvinītānāṃ vṛddhānām ātmavatām alolupānām adāmbhikānāṃ vṛttasādṛśyaṃ bhajeta
english_rendering: Dharma and adharma do not announce themselves; gods and ancestors do not point them out. Look to conduct praised by disciplined, mature, self-controlled, non-greedy, sincere people.
context_and_limits: Not pure individual reason: the solution is ethically qualified communal judgment. Also numbered 1.20.6–8 in another scheme.

sanskrit_iast: sāṃkhyaṃ yogo lokāyataṃ ca ity ānvīkṣikī | dharmādharmau trayyām arthānarthau vārttāyāṃ nayānayau daṇḍanītyāṃ balābale caitāsāṃ hetubhir anvīkṣamāṇā lokasyopakaroti | pradīpaḥ sarvavidyānām upāyaḥ sarvakarmaṇām | āśrayaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ śaśvad ānvīkṣikī matā
english_rendering: Inquiry examines dharma and adharma, gain and loss, policy, strength and weakness by reasons; it is a lamp for all sciences and a means for all actions.
context_and_limits: Classical defense of ānvīkṣikī, including Sāṃkhya, Yoga and Lokāyata.

sanskrit_iast: na kaṃcid avamanyeta sarvasya śṛṇuyān matam | bālasyāpy arthavad vākyam upayuñjīta paṇḍitaḥ
english_rendering: Despise no one; hear everyone’s view. A wise person should use a meaningful statement even from a child.
context_and_limits: A direct status-independent rule for evaluating speech by content.

sanskrit_iast: sahādhyāyino hy amātyaṃ parīkṣeran ... pratyakṣaparokṣānumeyā hi rājavṛttiḥ
english_rendering: Ministers should be tested through informed witnesses; royal affairs are known through direct observation, report, and inference.
context_and_limits: Institutional testing and evidence; practical rather than spiritual.

sanskrit_iast: na devacaritaṃ caret
english_rendering: Do not imitate the conduct of gods.
context_and_limits: Very concise parallel to Bhāgavata 10.33.30–31.

sanskrit_iast: na daivamātrapramāṇānāṃ kāryasiddhiḥ
english_rendering: Those who rely on fate alone do not accomplish their task.
context_and_limits: Practical warning against single-factor fatalism.

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣaparokṣānumānaiḥ kāryāṇi parīkṣet
english_rendering: Examine undertakings by direct evidence, indirect report, and inference.
context_and_limits: Compact practical epistemology.

sanskrit_iast: bālād api yuktam arthaṃ śṛṇuyāt
english_rendering: Hear a reasonable point even from a child.
context_and_limits: Status does not determine truth.

sanskrit_iast: yuktiyuktaṃ vaco grāhyaṃ na vaco gurugauravāt
english_rendering: Accept a reasoned statement, not a statement merely because of reverence for a guru.
context_and_limits: Exact parallel of the Yājñavalkyaśikṣā manuscript wording; Cāṇakya collections are composite and edition-dependent.
verification: Verified digitized edition; collection attribution qualified

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni
english_rendering: Perception, inference, and reliable testimony are means of valid cognition.
context_and_limits: Testimony is one pramāṇa among three, not necessarily subordinate.

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣānumānopamānaśabdāḥ pramāṇāni
english_rendering: Perception, inference, comparison, and testimony are means of knowledge.
context_and_limits: Nyāya’s four-pramāṇa framework.

sanskrit_iast: āptopadeśaḥ śabdaḥ
english_rendering: Testimony is the instruction of a trustworthy competent person.
context_and_limits: Authority depends on āptatva, not a title alone.

sanskrit_iast: dṛṣṭam anumānam āptavacanaṃ ca sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt | trividhaṃ pramāṇam iṣṭaṃ prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇād dhi
english_rendering: Perception, inference, and trustworthy testimony are accepted; an object is established through valid means of knowledge.
context_and_limits: Plural epistemology, not anti-scriptural.

sanskrit_iast: bhūtato 'bhūtato vāpi sṛjyamāne samā śrutiḥ | niścitaṃ yuktiyuktaṃ ca yat tad bhavati netarat
english_rendering: Scriptural creation language can be read in different ways; the settled meaning is the one supported by reasoning, not another.
context_and_limits: Context reconciles apparently conflicting creation passages.

sanskrit_iast: api pauruṣam ādeyaṃ śāstraṃ ced yuktibodhakam | anyad ārṣam api tyājyaṃ bhāvyaṃ nyāyaikasevinā
english_rendering: Even a human-authored text may be accepted if it teaches with reason; even a sage-attributed text should be left if otherwise, by one devoted to sound reasoning.
context_and_limits: Older Mokṣopāya recension; one of the strongest direct passages.

sanskrit_iast: yuktiyuktam upādeyaṃ vacanaṃ bālakād api | anyat tṛṇam iva tyājyam apy uktaṃ padmajanmanā
english_rendering: Accept a reasoned statement even from a child; discard an unreasonable one like straw even if spoken by Brahmā.
context_and_limits: Later Yoga Vāsiṣṭha recension; direct status-independent evaluation.

sanskrit_iast: cittasya śuddhaye karma na tu vastūpalabdhaye | vastusiddhir vicāreṇa na kiṃcit karmakoṭibhiḥ ... samyagvicārataḥ siddhā rajjutattvāvadhāraṇā
english_rendering: Actions purify the mind, but reality is established through inquiry; correct investigation resolves illusion as surely as recognizing a rope ends fear of a snake.
context_and_limits: Traditional Advaita inquiry under a teacher.

sanskrit_iast: vastusvarūpaṃ sphuṭabodhacakṣuṣā svenaiva vedyaṃ na tu paṇḍitena | candrasvarūpaṃ nijacakṣuṣaiva jñātavyam anyair avagamyate kim
english_rendering: Reality must be known through one’s own clear vision, not merely through a scholar—just as one must see the moon with one’s own eyes.
context_and_limits: Direct-experience emphasis within a guru-led text.

sanskrit_iast: vāgvaikharī śabdajharī śāstravyākhyānakauśalam | vaiduṣyaṃ viduṣāṃ tadvat bhuktaye na tu muktaye ... ajñānasarpadaṣṭasya brahmajñānauṣadhaṃ vinā | kim u vedaiś ca śāstraiś ca kim u mantraiḥ kim auṣadhaiḥ
english_rendering: Eloquence, torrents of words, and skill in explaining scripture may bring enjoyment, not liberation; texts and formulas alone do not cure ignorance.
context_and_limits: Rejects sufficiency of verbal scholarship, not the need for teaching.

sanskrit_iast: śrutipramāṇaikamateḥ svadharmaniṣṭhā ... svānubhūtyā svayaṃ jñātvā svam ātmānam akhaṇḍitam
english_rendering: Scripture, reasoning, the teacher’s statement, and direct experience converge; the disciple must realize the undivided Self personally.
context_and_limits: Conclusion of a strongly guru-centered Advaita work.

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣānumānāptavacanam iti pramāṇāni
english_rendering: Perception, inference, and trustworthy testimony are means of knowledge.
context_and_limits: Śaiva school’s pramāṇa statement; āgama remains authoritative.

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣam anumānaṃ ca āgamas tasya sādhanam ... yuktijanyaṃ tu vijñānam anumānikam ucyate
english_rendering: Perception, inference, and āgama are instruments of knowledge; inferential cognition is generated through reasoning.
context_and_limits: Technical Pāñcarātra epistemology, not equal weighting of all sources.

sanskrit_iast: buddhimān ātmanaḥ kāryagurulāghavaṃ karmaphalam anubandhaṃ deśakālau ca viditvā yuktidarśanād bhiṣag bubhūṣuḥ śāstram evāditaḥ parīkṣeta
english_rendering: A thoughtful would-be physician should first examine the medical text through reasoning, considering purpose, consequences, place, and time.
context_and_limits: Direct instruction to test the śāstra before selecting a teacher.

sanskrit_iast: tato 'nantaram ācāryaṃ parīkṣeta ... paryavadātaśrutaṃ paridṛṣṭakarmāṇaṃ dakṣam ... anahaṅkṛtam anasūyakam akopanaṃ kleśakṣamaṃ śiṣyavatsalam adhyāpakaṃ jñāpanasamarthaṃ ca
english_rendering: Next one should examine the teacher: learned, experienced, competent, unpretentious, free from envy and anger, patient, caring toward students, and able to explain.
context_and_limits: A detailed teacher-selection test.

sanskrit_iast: manāḥpurasarābhir vāgbhiḥ sūtram anukraman punaḥ punar āvartayet | buddhvā samyag anupraviśyārthatattvaṃ svadoṣaparihārārthaṃ paradoṣapramāṇārthaṃ ca
english_rendering: Repeat a teaching only with attention and after entering its meaning, so as to correct one’s own errors and assess errors in others.
context_and_limits: Understanding, not rote repetition, is the stated aim.

sanskrit_iast: na ca nigrahabhayād udvijet nigṛhya cainaṃ na hṛṣyet | na ca mohād ekāntagrāhī syān na cāviditam artham anuvarṇayet
english_rendering: Do not fear being refuted or boast after refuting another; do not become one-sided through delusion or speak about what you do not know.
context_and_limits: Explicit debate ethics and anti-dogmatism.

sanskrit_iast: siddhānto nāma sa parīkṣakair bahuvidhaṃ parīkṣya hetubhiś ca sādhayitvā sthāpyate nirṇayaḥ
english_rendering: An established conclusion is a determination tested in many ways by examiners and established through reasons.
context_and_limits: One of the clearest classical definitions of a tested conclusion.

sanskrit_iast: tāḥ sarvāḥ samavekṣyāvekṣya sarvaṃ vākyaṃ brūyāt | nāprakṛtakam aśāstram aparīkṣitam asādhakam ākulam avyāpakaṃ vā | sarvaṃ ca hetumad brūyāt
english_rendering: After examining all sides, do not state what is irrelevant, unexamined, unproved, confused, or overbroad; everything stated should have reasons.
context_and_limits: Strong rule for responsible argument.

sanskrit_iast: rogam ādau parīkṣeta tato 'nantaram auṣadham | tataḥ karma bhiṣak paścāj jñānapūrvaṃ samācaret
english_rendering: First examine the disease, then select the medicine, and only afterward act with knowledge.
context_and_limits: Clinical sequence; practical evidence rather than authority.

sanskrit_iast: cintyaṃ vicāryam ūhyaṃ ca ... ūho vicāraś ca tataḥ paraṃ buddhiḥ pravartate
english_rendering: Reasoning and deliberation operate on what is to be thought through and inferred; intellect proceeds after inquiry.
context_and_limits: Technical psychology of reasoning; thematic support.

sanskrit_iast: adhigatam apy adhyayanam aprabhāṣitam arthataḥ kharasya candanabhāra iva kevalaṃ pariśramakaraṃ bhavati | yathā kharaś candanabhāravāhī bhārasya vettā na tu candanasya | evaṃ hi śāstrāṇi bahūny adhītya cārtheṣu mūḍhāḥ kharavad vahanti
english_rendering: Study without understanding the meaning is like a donkey carrying sandalwood: it knows the weight, not the fragrance.
context_and_limits: Critique of rote textual accumulation.

sanskrit_iast: ekaṃ śāstram adhīyāno na vidyāc chāstraniścayam | tasmād bahuśrutaḥ śāstraṃ vijānīyāc cikitsakaḥ
english_rendering: By studying only one science, one cannot gain certainty; therefore a physician should study widely.
context_and_limits: Direct comparative-study principle, within medicine.

sanskrit_iast: paricaryāyaśolābhalipsuḥ śiṣyād gurur na hi | kṛpāsindhuḥ susampūrṇaḥ sarvasattvopakārakaḥ || niḥspṛhaḥ ... sarvasaṃśayasaṃchettā ... gurur āhṛtaḥ
english_rendering: One who desires service, fame, or gain from a disciple is not a guru; a guru is selfless, compassionate, and able to cut doubts.
context_and_limits: Strong negative and positive qualification test.

sanskrit_iast: mahākulaprasūto 'pi sarvayajñeṣu dīkṣitaḥ | sahasraśākhādhyāyī ca na guruḥ syād avaiṣṇavaḥ
english_rendering: High birth, many initiations, and mastery of a thousand Vedic branches do not by themselves qualify one as guru.
context_and_limits: Sectarian Vaiṣṇava criterion; useful only for the narrower point that status and learning are insufficient.

sanskrit_iast: iti tayoḥ parīkṣā cānyonyam ekābdaṃ sahavāsataḥ | vyavahārasvabhāvānubhavenaivābhijāyate || tayor vatsaravāsena jñātānyonyasvabhāvayoḥ | gurutā śiṣyatā ceti nānyathaiveti niścayaḥ
english_rendering: Guru and prospective disciple should test one another through a year of living together and observing conduct and character before establishing the relationship.
context_and_limits: Mutual testing; an unusually concrete procedural safeguard.

sanskrit_iast: yo vakti nyāyarahitam anyāyena śṛṇoti yaḥ | tāv ubhau narakaṃ ghoraṃ vrajataḥ kālam akṣayam
english_rendering: The one who teaches without valid warrant and the one who receives such teaching wrongly are both condemned.
context_and_limits: Nyāya here can mean correct scriptural/moral warrant, not merely formal logic; quotation location varies in later works.

sanskrit_iast: śaktihīnaṃ guruṃ prāpya śiṣyasiddhiḥ kutaḥ priye | mūle naṣṭe drume devi kutaḥ puṣpaphalādikam ... pratyakṣapratyayo yatra na syād iha janmani
english_rendering: How can a disciple attain success from a guru without power? If the root is destroyed, whence flowers and fruit? The text further asks for present-life experiential assurance.
context_and_limits: The manuscript is damaged in this passage; wording and segmentation are editorially uncertain.

sanskrit_iast: āmodārthī yathā bhṛṅgaḥ puṣpāt puṣpāntaraṃ vrajet | vijñānārthī tathā śiṣyo guror gurvantaraṃ vrajet
english_rendering: As a bee seeking fragrance moves from flower to flower, a disciple seeking fuller knowledge may move from one guru to another.
context_and_limits: Abhinavagupta quotes an earlier scriptural verse; also repeated at Tantrāloka 22.45–46.
verification: Verified digital Sanskrit; quoted source family

sanskrit_iast: śaktihīnaṃ guruṃ prāpya mokṣajñāne kathaṃ śrayet | naṣṭamūle drume devi kutaḥ puṣpaphalādikam
english_rendering: How could liberation-knowledge be obtained through a guru without power? If a tree’s root is ruined, whence flowers and fruit?
context_and_limits: Quoted Tantric criterion; parallel of Timirodghāṭana and Kubjikāmata.

sanskrit_iast: guravo bahavaḥ santi śiṣyavittāpahārakāḥ | durlabho 'yaṃ gurur devi śiṣyaduḥkhāpahārakaḥ
english_rendering: Many gurus take a disciple’s wealth; rare is the guru who removes the disciple’s suffering.
context_and_limits: Variants read citta-, hṛttāpa-, santāpa-, or duḥkha-; citation needs edition-specific checking.

sanskrit_iast: śaktihīnaṃ guruṃ prāpya śiṣye muktiḥ kutaḥ priye | mūlacchinne yathā vṛkṣe kutaḥ puṣpaphalādikam
english_rendering: How can a disciple gain liberation from a guru lacking power, just as a severed tree cannot bear flowers or fruit?
context_and_limits: Parallel in the “powerless guru” textual family.
verification: Verified digital Sanskrit; edition spelling normalized

sanskrit_iast: purāṇam ity eva na sādhu sarvaṃ na cāpi kāvyaṃ navam ity avadyam | santaḥ parīkṣyānyatarad bhajante mūḍhaḥ parapratyayaneyabuddhiḥ
english_rendering: Not everything is good merely because it is old, nor bad because it is new. The discerning examine and choose; a fool’s judgment is led by others.
context_and_limits: Classical literature, not śruti or smṛti; exceptionally direct.

sanskrit_iast: nānā mataṃ maharṣīṇāṃ sādhūnāṃ yogināṃ tathā | dṛṣṭvā nirvedam āpannaḥ ko na śāmyati mānavaḥ
english_rendering: Seeing the many differing views of sages, saints, and yogins, what thoughtful person would not become detached from opinion?
context_and_limits: Late Advaita text; promotes dispassion more than a method of proof.

sanskrit_iast: yuktiyuktaṃ vaco grāhyaṃ bālād api śukād api | ayuktam api na grāhyaṃ sākṣād api bṛhaspateḥ
english_rendering: Accept a reasoned statement even from a child—or a parrot; do not accept an unreasonable one even from Bṛhaspati himself.
context_and_limits: Widely circulated but exact classical source remains unverified; not to be cited as secure scripture.
verification: Uncertain attribution; included only as flagged lead
